text:
olivia: Hey team — quick infra question. We're adding a logging sidecar (namespace=telemetry) that needs to envelope-encrypt logs with our CMK (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333444:key/abc123). Using IRSA (k8s sa annotated -> IAM role) — what's the minimal Terraform wiring so the sidecar can Encrypt/Decrypt but only when EncryptionContext service=sidecar-proxy? I'm trying a grant but not sure about key policy interplay. Example I'm experimenting with:
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "sidecar" {
  name               = "sidecar-proxy-grant"
  key_id             = aws_kms_key.logs_key.key_id
  grantee_principal  = aws_iam_role.sidecar_role.arn
  operations         = ["Encrypt", "Decrypt"]
  constraints = {
    encryption_context_subset = {"service" = "sidecar-proxy"}
  }
}
```
Is that sufficient, or do we also need to alter the key policy to explicitly allow the role or the Terraform service account to create grants? Also, will the constraint work if the grantee principal is the IRSA role (i.e., requests come via sts:AssumeRole)?

Thanks — want to avoid giving broad kms:* on the key.

---
dan: Grants are OK but remember: CreateGrant must be called by someone allowed by the key policy. So TF (or the deployer) needs kms:CreateGrant on the key in its IAM permission and the key policy must allow the principal that runs TF to manage grants. The grant itself limits runtime ops as you wrote.

If you want long-lived, consider embedding an explicit statement in the key policy that allows the sidecar role to use Encrypt/Decrypt with the encryptioncontext condition. Grants can be revoked, and are more ephemeral.

Example key policy snippet (very small):
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowSidecarUse",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/sidecar-role" },
  "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "kms:EncryptionContext:service": "sidecar-proxy" } }
}
```
sasha: a few practical notes: 1) encryption_context_subset is supported on grants, but name the map keys exactly. TF's aws_kms_grant expects constraints as a block; your HCL looks fine. 2) IRSA roles are normal IAM roles when assumed, so KMS checks the role ARN — constraints will work. 3) make sure the role's session tags or external ID (if you use them) aren't required by the key policy unless you add matching conditions.

jamal: deployment sequencing gotchas — when TF creates the grant, it will ask KMS to create it using whatever principal runs TF. If you run TF from a CI role that doesn't have kms:CreateGrant, plan will fail. Either give the CI role CreateGrant OR apply a key policy change first that allows the CI/principal to manage grants. Also, grants are sticky: if you recreate the key or rotation happens you might need to re-issue.

infra-bot: FYI — earlier today I logged a terraform plan failure in staging when we tried to create a grant without kms:CreateGrant. See link: https://ci.internal/plan/8675309 :warning:

terra-plan-bot: plan excerpt:
```
+ aws_kms_grant.sidecar (new)
+ aws_kms_key_policy.logs_key_policy (updated)
```
If you want atomicity, attach the policy change first then the grant, or use depends_on to force order.

olivia: thanks — plan is: 1) add minimal key policy allowing our CI deploy role to manage grants, 2) TF creates aws_kms_grant with encryption_context_subset for service=sidecar-proxy, 3) keep a short TTL on grants? any suggestions on TTL revocation? :thinking_face:

dan: you can set retires on grants? KMS grants support retiring by the principal that created them, but TTLs aren't native. Common pattern: create long-lived key policy allowance + short-lived role permissions elsewhere. For revocation control, you can track the grant ID returned by TF and explicitly revoke when decommissioning.

sasha: agree. If you really need expiration, add a small Lambda that audits grants and revokes based on tag/creation-time. Otherwise key-policy-based restrictions are simpler and more auditable. :+1:

olivia: perfect — I'll update the TF to: a) create a small policy statement for the CI principal allowing kms:CreateGrant/kms:RetireGrant, b) create the aws_kms_grant with encryption_context_subset, and c) add depends_on so policy updates before grant. I'll post the PR in ~30m for a quick review. Thanks! :rocket:
